# Introduction

I install the packages needed and import the **same dataset**
(`students.sav`) from different sources, then show how each library helps
to read, inspect and analyse the data:

1. An **SPSS file** (`students.sav`), my original dataset (package **haven**)
2. A **Stata file** (`students.dta`) (package **haven**)
3. A **CSV file** (`students.csv`) (base R)
4. A **JSON file** (`students.json`) (package **jsonlite**)
5. A **database** (SQLite, `students.sqlite`) (packages **DBI** and **RSQLite**)
6. A **public API** (package **jsonlite**)

> Keep `students.sav` in the same folder as this `.Rmd` file.
> The other files are created from it by the code below.

---

# Packages

| Package | Why we need it |
|---|---|
| haven | Read and write SPSS and Stata files |
| dplyr | Select, filter and summarise data |
| jsonlite | Read and write JSON, and call web APIs |
| DBI | Common interface for databases |
| RSQLite | SQLite database driver (no server needed) |
| knitr | Print neat tables |

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# Run this ONCE in the console (not every time you knit)
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
install.packages(c(
  "rmarkdown", 
  "knitr", 
  "haven", 
  "dplyr",
                   
  "jsonlite", 
  "DBI", 
  "RSQLite"))
```

```{r packages}
library(haven)     # SPSS / Stata files
library(dplyr)     # data manipulation
library(jsonlite)  # JSON and APIs
library(DBI)       # database interface
library(RSQLite)   # SQLite driver
library(knitr)     # tables
```

---

# Source 1: SPSS file (.sav)

**Function name:** `read_sav()`

**Short description:** From the **haven** package. It reads an SPSS file into R
and keeps the variable labels and value labels.

**What we are doing with it:** Importing my dataset `students.sav`.

```{r spss-import}
students_spss <- read_sav("students.sav")

dim(students_spss)   # rows and columns
```

The file has many variables, so I select the ones used in this assignment.
Each variable has a label that explains its meaning.

```{r spss-select}
vars <- c("CNTRY", "AGEA", "GNDR", "EDUYRS", "HAPPY",
          "STFLIFE", "TRSTPLT", "TRSTPRL")

students <- students_spss |> select(all_of(vars))

# Variable labels
data.frame(variable = vars,
           label = sapply(students, function(x) attr(x, "label"))) |>
  kable(row.names = FALSE, caption = "Variables used and their labels")
```

```{r spss-inspect}
head(students)
str(students)
summary(students)
```

Missing values per variable:

```{r spss-missing}
colSums(is.na(students))
```

---

# Source 2: Stata file (.dta)

**Function name:** `write_dta()`, `read_dta()`

**Short description:** From **haven**. `write_dta()` saves a data frame as a Stata
file and `read_dta()` reads a Stata file into R.

**What we are doing with it:** Exporting the data to `students.dta`, then importing it back.

```{r dta}
write_dta(students, "students.dta")

students_dta <- read_dta("students.dta")

dim(students_dta)
head(students_dta)
summary(students_dta)
```

---

# Source 3: CSV file

**Function name:** `write.csv()`, `read.csv()`

**Short description:** Base R functions. `write.csv()` saves a data frame as a
comma-separated text file and `read.csv()` reads it back, using the first row
as column names.

**What we are doing with it:** CSV cannot store labels, so I first convert the
coded variables (country and gender) to readable text and the others to numbers.

```{r csv-prepare}
students_clean <- students |>
  mutate(CNTRY = as.character(as_factor(CNTRY)),
         GNDR  = as.character(as_factor(GNDR)),
         across(c(AGEA, EDUYRS, HAPPY, STFLIFE, TRSTPLT, TRSTPRL), as.numeric))

head(students_clean)
```

```{r csv}
write.csv(students_clean, "students.csv", row.names = FALSE)

students_csv <- read.csv("students.csv")

dim(students_csv)
head(students_csv)
summary(students_csv)
```

---

# Source 4: JSON file

**Function name:** `write_json()`, `fromJSON()`

**Short description:** From **jsonlite**. `write_json()` saves a data frame as
JSON and `fromJSON()` reads a JSON file into a data frame.

**What we are doing with it:** Exporting the clean data to `students.json` and importing it.

```{r json}
write_json(students_clean, "students.json", pretty = TRUE)

students_json <- fromJSON("students.json")

dim(students_json)
head(students_json)
str(students_json)
```

---

# Source 5: Database (SQLite)

**Function name:** `dbConnect()`, `dbWriteTable()`, `dbGetQuery()`, `dbDisconnect()`

**Short description:** From **DBI**. `dbConnect()` opens a connection,
`dbWriteTable()` saves a data frame as a table, `dbGetQuery()` runs an SQL query
and returns a data frame, and `dbDisconnect()` closes the connection.

**What we are doing with it:** Saving the data in a SQLite database and
importing it with SQL queries. (SQLite works on any computer without a server.
For MySQL/MariaDB, only the `dbConnect()` line changes. See Assignment 2.)

```{r db-connect}
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "students.sqlite")

dbWriteTable(con, "students", students_clean, overwrite = TRUE)

dbListTables(con)
```

```{r db-import}
# Import the whole table
students_db <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM students")
dim(students_db)
head(students_db)
```

SQL queries return exactly the information we ask for:

```{r db-sql}
dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT CNTRY AS country,
         COUNT(*) AS respondents,
         ROUND(AVG(AGEA), 1) AS mean_age,
         ROUND(AVG(STFLIFE), 2) AS mean_life_satisfaction
  FROM students
  GROUP BY CNTRY
  ORDER BY respondents DESC") |>
  kable(caption = "Summary by country (SQL query)")
```

```{r db-close}
dbDisconnect(con)
```

---

# Source 6: Public API

**Function name:** `fromJSON()` with a web address

**Short description:** `fromJSON()` can read JSON directly from a web address (API).

**What we are doing with it:** Importing a list of users from a public test API.
This needs internet; if it is unavailable, a message is shown instead.

```{r api}
users <- tryCatch(
  fromJSON("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users"),
  error = function(e) { message("API not reachable: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }
)

if (!is.null(users)) {
  print(dim(users))
  head(users[, c("id", "name", "username", "email")])
}
```

---

# Checking that all sources give the same data

```{r check}
data.frame(
  source = c("SPSS", "Stata", "CSV", "JSON", "SQLite"),
  rows   = c(nrow(students_spss), nrow(students_dta), nrow(students_csv),
             nrow(students_json), nrow(students_db)),
  columns_used = c(ncol(students), ncol(students_dta), ncol(students_csv),
                   ncol(students_json), ncol(students_db))
) |> kable(caption = "Rows and columns imported from each source")
```

---

# Using the libraries on the data

Once imported, **dplyr** and base R work the same way on every source.

```{r analysis}
students_csv |>
  filter(!is.na(GNDR)) |>
  group_by(GNDR) |>
  summarise(respondents = n(),
            mean_age = round(mean(AGEA, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            mean_life_satisfaction = round(mean(STFLIFE, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            mean_trust_politicians = round(mean(TRSTPLT, na.rm = TRUE), 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Key indicators by gender")
```

```{r plot}
hist(students_csv$STFLIFE, breaks = 0:10 - 0.5, col = "steelblue",
     main = "Satisfaction with life (0-10)",
     xlab = "Life satisfaction", ylab = "Respondents")
```

# Conclusion

| Package | Function(s) | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| haven | `read_sav()`, `write_dta()`, `read_dta()` | SPSS and Stata files |
| base R | `read.csv()`, `write.csv()` | CSV files |
| jsonlite | `fromJSON()`, `write_json()` | JSON files and APIs |
| DBI + RSQLite | `dbConnect()`, `dbGetQuery()` | Databases and SQL |
| dplyr | `select()`, `mutate()`, `group_by()`, `summarise()` | Data manipulation |

All six sources gave the same data in R, so the same analysis works on each one.
